base.text: The driver-based forecast significantly outperformed the naive extrapolation across all three key metrics. Revenue came in at 24811 against the driver-based forecast of 25585.2, missing by 3.1 percent, compared to the naive forecast's 5.5 percent miss. Operating profit actual of 2056 exceeded the driver-based forecast of 1750.0 by 14.9 percent, while the naive forecast understated it by 22.3 percent. Free cash flow of 1106.4 came in only 3.4 percent below the driver-based forecast of 1069.2, whereas the naive forecast overstated it by 14.8 percent, demonstrating that the granular driver approach captured the underlying business dynamics more accurately than top-down extrapolation.

upside.text: Revenue came in modestly below the upside scenario at 24,811 versus a forecasted 25,822.1, an underperformance of 4.1 percent. Operating profit significantly outperformed the upside forecast, delivering 2,056 against the projected 2,024.4—a beat of 1.5 percent—suggesting better cost management than anticipated despite the revenue shortfall. Free cash flow of 1,106.4 fell short of the upside projection of 1,360.4 by 23.0 percent, driven primarily by a larger increase in working capital (757.1 in upside versus actual results) that offset the operating profit strength. The forecast's revenue miss was relatively modest, but the working capital swing materially constrained cash generation despite operational efficiency gains.

downside.text: Revenue came in below both forecasts, falling short of the naive extrapolation by 5.5% to 24,811, though it tracked much closer to the downside scenario at just 2.2% above plan. Operating profit significantly exceeded expectations across both frameworks—the actual 2,056 beat the naive forecast by 22.3% and the downside case by 28.0%—suggesting better cost management than either model anticipated. Free cash flow underperformed relative to both the naive forecast (missing by 14.8%) and the downside scenario (missing by 29.1%), indicating that cash conversion efficiency lagged despite the strong profit performance, likely driven by working capital dynamics not fully captured in the planning models.

wc_stress.text: Actual revenue came in at 24,811, below the naive extrapolation of 26,176.5 by 5.5%, though the working capital stress case predicted 25,585.2, missing by only 3.1%. Operating profit significantly outperformed both approaches: actual came in at 2,056, beating the naive forecast of 1,596.5 (which was off by -22.3%) and the stress case of 1,750.0 (off by -14.9%). Free cash flow of 1,106.4 fell short of the naive forecast of 1,270.2 by 14.8%, and the stress case projection of 429.6 substantially underestimated actual performance by 61.2%, driven primarily by the stress case's assumption of a large 1,474.9 working capital outflow that did not materialize.

margin_compression.text: Revenue came in below both forecasts, with actual revenue of 24811 versus the naive projection of 26176.5 (a 5.5% miss) and the margin compression scenario of 25585.2 (a 3.1% miss). Operating profit significantly exceeded expectations across the board: actual results of 2056 beat the naive forecast of 1596.5 by 22.3% and the margin compression scenario of 1238.3 by 39.8%, indicating materially stronger cost control or pricing than either scenario anticipated. Free cash flow of 1106.4 fell short of the naive forecast's 1270.2 (down 14.8%) and substantially underperformed the margin compression scenario's 693.1 (up 37.4%), suggesting that while profitability held up well, working capital management or capital allocation differed from both expectations. The divergence between profit and cash flow performance warrants investigation into working capital swings and capital deployment during the period.
